title: Example 14-4: Italics Retained for Unenclosed Stage Directions

illustrates.quote: Ignore font attributes used for stage directions, unless needed for distinction, e.g., when stage directions after a speaker’s name are not enclosed in punctuation. If text within stage directions requires emphasis for distinction, use the typeform indicator that best represents print emphasis of surrounding text.

blocks.speaker: MAMA
blocks.text: MAMA *hysterically:* But I can’t do anything about that!

print.notes: Speaker names in full capitalization (retained per 14.1.2); the stage direction immediately after each name (‘hysterically:’, ‘quietly:’) is NOT enclosed in punctuation, so its own italic font attribute is kept for distinction per 14.4.1c, up to and including the colon that has no space before it.
print.printFeatures: Full capitalization for speaker names; italics on the unenclosed stage-direction word immediately following each name; dialogue in regular type.

braille.notes: 1-3 margins for each speech (14.5.1a); the italic word indicator (.1) covers 'hysterically:'/'quietly:' up to the colon since there is no space before it; the colon itself is not a separate word.

resolution: A/B agreed on braille (byte-for-byte) and on the substance (speaker names all-caps, stage-direction word italicized, unenclosed); both, however, described the italics only in a prose `features`/`printFeatures` string rather than marking it in `text` itself. Per this repo's own established convention (emphasis marked in place with Emboss's *italic* cell-markup), `text` was rewritten to embed *hysterically:*/*quietly:* directly, with the colon inside the italic run (forward-translation confirms the colon must stay inside the italic segment to reproduce the given braille's single '3' terminator with no separate closing mark). illustrates.rule: A already had this right ('14.4.1c'); B's own '14.5.1c' is wrong (no such rule id is quoted at source lines 128-134) and was not used. Forward-translated through Emboss's translator (two {type:'play', subtype:'prose'} blocks, 1-3 margins): EXACT MATCH (see differences.md).
